verdict.rationale: The Pipecat Cloud OpenAPI spec says its private API manages "regions", which suggests some first-party control over where agents run. The open-source framework is also documented as self-hostable, so data can stay on infrastructure the user chooses. Nothing explicitly describes data-residency guarantees or storage-region selection, so this is only a thin, glancing signal. Missing for 10: documented region selection for stored data such as recordings, transcripts and logs; a list of available regions; data-residency or compliance commitments; independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can choose where my data is stored (region/residency)

citations.quote: The private API (/v1...) manages agents, secrets, builds, regions, and organization settings.
the open-source voice-agent framework is real, pip-installable, and self-hostable
